title: SilentProcessExit monitor configured with an interpreter or staging path
description: Detects a machine-wide SilentProcessExit MonitorProcess value whose command starts with a selected interpreter or a rooted staging path.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may configure a SilentProcessExit monitor command to launch an interpreter or payload from a staging directory when the monitored process exits.
hypothesis.rationale: The value is configuration evidence; GlobalFlag, ReportingMode, the monitored exit and actual process execution are not proven.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Detects a machine-wide SilentProcessExit MonitorProcess value whose command starts with a selected interpreter or a rooted staging path.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint registry events

triage.summary: The value is configuration evidence; GlobalFlag, ReportingMode, the monitored exit and actual process execution are not proven.
steps: Inspect the complete MonitorProcess command and the exact application key, actor and parent process.
Verify the associated Image File Execution Options GlobalFlag and SilentProcessExit ReportingMode, then check observed monitor execution.
Confirm an approved diagnostic owner and investigate the referenced executable and adjacent persistence changes.
false_positives: Authorized crash diagnostics, debugging or compatibility tooling using a selected interpreter or staging path.

validation.expected_outcome: Match the bounded event, key/action/path or successful operation combination; reject one-field mutations, lookalikes and absent required fields. Synthetic tests do not establish live telemetry or production performance.

limitations: The value is configuration evidence; GlobalFlag, ReportingMode, the monitored exit and actual process execution are not proven.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
